description.narrative: Following the escalation of hostilities on 2 March, over 667,000 people have registered as internally displaced across Lebanon, with nearly 120,000 sheltering in collective sites and many more living in unsafe or overcrowded conditions. Access to clean water, sanitation, food, and essential services is severely strained, and protection risks—particularly for women, girls, migrants, refugees, and LGBTQIA+ individuals—are rising. In response, Oxfam and partners ShareQ and Nabad are delivering integrated Food Security, WASH,and Multi-Purpose Cash (MPC) assistance across Beirut, Mount Lebanon (Barja and Shehim), and South Lebanon (Saida and Jezzine). Theproject will support 8,744 displaced people inside and outside collective shelters. The response includes daily hot meals and ready-to-eat food kits for families without cooking facilities, emergency cash assistance for highly vulnerable households, hygiene and menstrual kits (including adapted kits for persons with disabilities), and water trucking to ensure safe water access in underserved shelters. All activities follow SPHERE and sector standards and integrate gender and protection measures, including GBV-sensitive approaches and inclusive targeting. Oxfam coordinates closely with local authorities, UN agencies, and humanitarian partners to avoid duplication and ensure a timely, effective response that addresses urgent needs while safeguarding dignity and rights

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam has been working in Lebanon since 2006; it has a regional Gender Justice Hub that administers a regional gender justice programme and a Lebanon programme that focuses on three thematic areas of work: Humanitarian, Economic Justice, and Active Citizenship <(><<)>(><(><<)><(><<)>)>(><(><<)>(><(>&<)><(><<)>)><(><<)>(><(><<)><(><<)>)>)> Governance. Over the course of the past three years, Oxfam in Lebanon has integrated its humanitarian and development programming into a #one programme approach#, as described in the Oxfam Country Strategy. The humanitarian component of the strategy looks at the continuation of life-saving WaSH service provision, protection services and cash assistance, while in parallel the development programs, in collaboration with local authorities and civil society, aim to address theunderlying root causes of inequality and poverty over the longer-term, including through policy change. Our vision is that, by the end of 2021, marginalized women and men (Lebanese, Palestinian and Syrian populations including refugees) are protected and empowered to enjoy their basic rights, enabling them to live in dignity within a more equitable society. Oxfam in Lebanon has a main office in Beirut, and two operational offices in Zahle (Bekaa governance) and Tripoli (North governance).
